title: Super Mario
tagline: A System One model plays a platform game several times a second, and you watch its browser.
description: Full Screen Mario runs in a headless browser inside this deployment. The System One base reads the game's own state each step as a few literal sentences (where Mario is, what is ahead and how far) and chooses one control to hold, a few hundred milliseconds a decision, with no screenshot and no text generation. The left pane streams the browser the model is playing in; the right pane is the run's conversation, every decision with the game's reply. Credits: the game is Full Screen Mario, played at supermarioplay.com; the browser is driven with Browser Use (MIT); the model is TypeSafe's Jev through OpenRouter.

harness.name: Super Mario
harness.system_prompt:
You play a side-scrolling platform game as Mario, deciding several times a second. Each action sets the keys for the next moment and they stay set until you change them: run_right holds right and run; jump_right holds right, run and jump; jump holds jump alone; walk_left holds left; wait lets every key go. Keep moving right.

Facts, measured on this game: a decision lands about every third of a second, and at a full run Mario covers about 3 tiles between decisions. A jump held for one decision clears 3 tiles, for two decisions 4 tiles; the jump key must be let go (run_right or wait) before Mario can jump again. A running jump lands about 9 tiles on. A pipe 4 tiles tall is cleared only from a run, leaving the ground 2 to 3 tiles before it with the jump held for three decisions; from against it, or from standing, it is never cleared, so if Mario is stopped at one, walk_left for two decisions, then run_right, then jump_right at 2 to 3 tiles. A gap is crossed by a running jump from its edge; a standing jump falls in. An enemy walking at Mario is safest let under a standing jump: wait until it is about one tile away, then jump; a running jump taken with it 2 tiles away hits it. Under a row of blocks a running jump hits the blocks and drops onto whatever is below, so let the first enemy under a standing jump. A question block is hit from below by a jump started 1 to 1.5 tiles before it at a run, and pays a coin. Enemies behind Mario are outrun.

When Mario has just died, wait. Finish when the level is cleared. Escalate when Mario has no lives left.
harness.$comment: system_prompt carries the measured facts of this game; the environment executes key states and times nothing. max_step: a decision every third of a second, the level takes a few hundred, and a death costs the way back.

session.$comment: One session is one run of the game. The frame the page streams is frame.jpg in the session's workspace, written by the environment about twenty times a second from the browser's own screencast.
